claim: TMEM16F is activated by elevated intracellular Ca2+
source: TMEM16F is activated by elevated intracellular Ca2+, and functions as a small-conductance ion channel and as a phospholipid scramblase.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript showing Ca2+-dependent activation.

claim: TMEM16F functions as a small-conductance ion channel
source: TMEM16F is activated by elevated intracellular Ca2+, and functions as a small-conductance ion channel and as a phospholipid scramblase.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by electrophysiological recordings throughout the manuscript.

claim: TMEM16F functions as a phospholipid scramblase
source: TMEM16F is activated by elevated intracellular Ca2+, and functions as a small-conductance ion channel and as a phospholipid scramblase.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Mouse TMEM16F has been reported as a cation-, anion-, or non-selective ion channel without a definite conclusion
source: In contrast to its paralogs, the TMEM16A/B calcium-activated chloride channels, mouse TMEM16F has been reported as a cation-, anion-, or non-selective ion channel, without a definite conclusion.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations to conflicting reports in the introduction.

claim: Q559K mutant shows no current rundown in excised patch
source: Starting with the Q559K mutant that shows no current rundown and less outward rectification in excised patch
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 1B,D.

claim: Q559K mutant shows less outward rectification in excised patch
source: Starting with the Q559K mutant that shows no current rundown and less outward rectification in excised patch
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 1F.

claim: TMEM16F Q559K channel shifted its ion selectivity in response to the change of intracellular Ca2+ concentration
source: we found that the channel shifted its ion selectivity in response to the change of intracellular Ca2+ concentration, with an increased permeability ratio of Cl- to Na+ (PCl-/PNa+) at a higher Ca2+ level.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated throughout the results section with reversal potential measurements.

claim: TMEM16F Q559K shows an increased permeability ratio of Cl- to Na+ (PCl-/PNa+) at a higher Ca2+ level
source: we found that the channel shifted its ion selectivity in response to the change of intracellular Ca2+ concentration, with an increased permeability ratio of Cl- to Na+ (PCl-/PNa+) at a higher Ca2+ level.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 1G showing reversal potential shifts.

claim: The gradual shift of relative ion permeability did not correlate with the channel activation state
source: The gradual shift of relative ion permeability did not correlate with the channel activation state.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 3 showing Erev remains unchanged during desensitization.

claim: The shift of relative ion permeability was indicative of an alteration of electrostatic field in the permeation pathway
source: Instead, it was indicative of an alteration of electrostatic field in the permeation pathway.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experiments with different divalent cations in Figure 5.

claim: The dynamic change of ion selectivity suggests a charge-screening mechanism for TMEM16F ion conduction
source: The dynamic change of ion selectivity suggests a charge-screening mechanism for TMEM16F ion conduction
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by the collective experimental evidence showing electrostatic modulation.

claim: TMEM16F mediates the exposure of phosphatidylserine to the cell surface when activated
source: When activated, TMEM16F mediates the exposure of phosphatidylserine, a lipid normally restricted to the inner leaflet of cell membrane lipid bilayer, to the cell surface (Suzuki et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to Suzuki et al., 2010.

claim: Phosphatidylserine is normally restricted to the inner leaflet of cell membrane lipid bilayer
source: When activated, TMEM16F mediates the exposure of phosphatidylserine, a lipid normally restricted to the inner leaflet of cell membrane lipid bilayer, to the cell surface (Suzuki et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is established knowledge in cell biology.

claim: Lipid scrambling initiates recruitment of tissue factors to the platelet surface for thrombin production to trigger blood coagulation
source: This process, known as lipid scrambling, initiates many physiological processes such as recruitment of tissue factors to the platelet surface for thrombin production to trigger blood coagulation and modulation of immune responses in T lymphocytes (Suzuki et al., 2010; Yang et al., 2012; Hu et al., 2016; Zaitseva et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to supporting literature.

claim: Lipid scrambling initiates modulation of immune responses in T lymphocytes
source: This process, known as lipid scrambling, initiates many physiological processes such as recruitment of tissue factors to the platelet surface for thrombin production to trigger blood coagulation and modulation of immune responses in T lymphocytes (Suzuki et al., 2010; Yang et al., 2012; Hu et al., 2016; Zaitseva et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to supporting literature.

claim: TMEM16F is a Ca2+-activated small-conductance ion channel
source: TMEM16F is also a Ca2+-activated small-conductance ion channel (Yang et al., 2012)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to Yang et al., 2012.

claim: TMEM16F channels recorded with excised-patch inside-out configuration are quickly activated by micromolar Ca2+
source: Recorded with excised-patch inside-out configuration, TMEM16F channels are quickly activated by micromolar Ca2+ and they are more permeable to cations (mainly physiological cations such as Na+, K+ and Ca2+) than to Cl- (Yang et al., 2012; Alvadia et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to Yang et al., 2012 and Alvadia et al., 2019.

claim: TMEM16F channels recorded with excised-patch inside-out configuration are more permeable to cations than to Cl-
source: Recorded with excised-patch inside-out configuration, TMEM16F channels are quickly activated by micromolar Ca2+ and they are more permeable to cations (mainly physiological cations such as Na+, K+ and Ca2+) than to Cl- (Yang et al., 2012; Alvadia et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to Yang et al., 2012 and Alvadia et al., 2019.

claim: TMEM16F whole-cell current is activated several minutes after cytoplasmic Ca2+ elevation
source: Surprisingly, many groups have reported that the TMEM16F whole-cell current is activated several minutes after cytoplasmic Ca2+ elevation, and it displays less cation-selectivity (Yu et al., 2015) or even higher permeability to Cl- than to Na+ (Grubb et al., 2013; Scudieri et al., 2015; Shimizu et al., 2013; Tian et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to multiple studies.

claim: TMEM16F whole-cell current displays less cation-selectivity or even higher permeability to Cl- than to Na+
source: Surprisingly, many groups have reported that the TMEM16F whole-cell current is activated several minutes after cytoplasmic Ca2+ elevation, and it displays less cation-selectivity (Yu et al., 2015) or even higher permeability to Cl- than to Na+ (Grubb et al., 2013; Scudieri et al., 2015; Shimizu et al., 2013; Tian et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to multiple studies.

claim: TMEM16F belongs to the mammalian TMEM16 membrane protein family with 10 members
source: TMEM16F belongs to the mammalian TMEM16 membrane protein family with 10 members (Whitlock and Hartzell, 2017; Falzone et al., 2018; Pedemonte and Galietta, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to review articles.

claim: TMEM16A and TMEM16B represent the only two canonical Ca2+-activated Cl- channels without lipid scrambling functions
source: The founding members TMEM16A (ANO1) and TMEM16B (ANO2) represent the only two canonical Ca2+-activated Cl- channels (CaCC) without lipid scrambling functions (Schroeder et al., 2008; Caputo et al., 2008; Yang et al., 2008; Stephan et al., 2009)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to multiple studies.

claim: Several mammalian TMEM16 homologs show a modest selectivity between cations and anions but with lipid scrambling capacities
source: while several other mammalian homologs show a modest selectivity between cations and anions but with lipid scrambling capacities (Suzuki et al., 2010; Suzuki et al., 2013; Gyobu et al., 2017; Le et al., 2019a; Watanabe et al., 2018)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to multiple studies.

claim: Mammalian TMEM16 proteins are dimeric
source: Mammalian TMEM16 proteins are dimeric, as revealed by structural analyses of TMEM16A, TMEM16F and TMEM16K via electron cryo-microscopy (cryo-EM) or crystallography (Alvadia et al., 2019; Paulino et al., 2017a; Paulino et al., 2017b; Bushell, 2018; Dang et al., 2017; Feng et al., 2019)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to structural studies.

claim: Each TMEM16 subunit contains a permeation pathway that works independently
source: and each subunit contains a permeation pathway that works independently (Paulino et al., 2017b; Lim et al., 2016; Jeng et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to functional studies.

claim: Each TMEM16A subunit contains 10 transmembrane helices (TM1 ~TM10)
source: For TMEM16A, each subunit contains 10 transmembrane helices (TM1 ~TM10)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is based on structural studies.

claim: The stabilization of TM6 by the binding of Ca2+ ions opens the TMEM16A permeation pathway
source: and the stabilization of TM6 by the binding of Ca2+ ions to the binding-pocket formed by acidic residues on TM6, TM7 and TM8 within the transmembrane domain opens the permeation pathway, composed of TM3-TM8 (Paulino et al., 2017a; Peters et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to structural and functional studies.

claim: The TMEM16A permeation pathway is composed of TM3-TM8
source: and the stabilization of TM6 by the binding of Ca2+ ions to the binding-pocket formed by acidic residues on TM6, TM7 and TM8 within the transmembrane domain opens the permeation pathway, composed of TM3-TM8 (Paulino et al., 2017a; Peters et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to structural studies.

claim: The positive electrostatic field introduced by Ca2+ ions bound to the binding-pocket contributes to anion accessibility to the TMEM16A pore
source: Recent studies suggested that, in addition to the pore-lining residues on TM3-TM8 along the TMEM16A permeation pathway for anion conduction, the positive electrostatic field introduced by the Ca2+ ions bound to the binding-pocket also contributes to anion accessibility to the pore (Lam and Dutzler, 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to Lam and Dutzler, 2018.

claim: TMEM16F current in inside-out excised patch exhibits rapid desensitization and rundown in high Ca2+
source: However, because TMEM16F current in inside-out excised patch exhibits rapid desensitization and rundown in high Ca2+ (Ye et al., 2018)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to Ye et al., 2018.

claim: Q559 in TMEM16F faces the ionic permeation pathway
source: In TMEM16F, glutamine 559 (Q559) faces the ionic permeation pathway
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is based on structural information.

claim: Lysine substitution of Q559 (Q559K) reduces the ratio of Na+ permeability to Cl- permeability (PNa+/PCl-)
source: and lysine substitution of this pore-lining residue (Q559K) reduces the ratio of Na+ permeability to Cl- permeability (PNa+/PCl-) (Yang et al., 2012; Alvadia et al., 2019; Feng et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to multiple studies.

claim: The current of Q559K persists with prolonged exposure of the excised patch to high intracellular Ca2+
source: Previous studies also show that the current of Q559K persists with prolonged exposure of the excised patch to high intracellular Ca2+, and that it displays reduced outward rectification (Alvadia et al., 2019; Nguyen et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to Alvadia et al., 2019 and Nguyen et al., 2019.

claim: Q559K displays reduced outward rectification
source: Previous studies also show that the current of Q559K persists with prolonged exposure of the excised patch to high intracellular Ca2+, and that it displays reduced outward rectification (Alvadia et al., 2019; Nguyen et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to Alvadia et al., 2019 and Nguyen et al., 2019.

claim: Wild-type mouse TMEM16F current was activated by intracellular Ca2+ in a dose-dependent manner
source: Recording from inside-out membrane patch held at +80 mV revealed that wild-type mouse TMEM16F current was activated by intracellular Ca2+ in a dose-dependent manner.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 1A,C.

claim: Wild-type TMEM16F current started to decrease when Ca2+ was higher than ~30 µM
source: The current started to decrease when Ca2+ was higher than ~30 µM, as a result of both desensitization and rundown (Figure 1A,C,D) (Ye et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1A,C,D.

claim: Desensitization is caused by degradation of PIP2 via membrane-tethered phospholipase activated by high intracellular Ca2+
source: Here, desensitization refers to a decreased sensitivity to Ca2+, caused by degradation of PIP2 via membrane-tethered phospholipase activated by high intracellular Ca2+.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and is based on previous work cited (Ye et al., 2018).

claim: Wild-type TMEM16F has V1/2 of 76 ± 11 mV in 15 µM Ca2+
source: Fitting to the sigmoidal conductance-voltage (G-V) relationship yielded V1/2 of 76 ± 11 mV in 15 µM Ca2+ for wild-type TMEM16F
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Wild-type TMEM16F in 15 µM Ca2+ is moderately selective for Na+ over Cl-
source: Consistent with previous reports (Yang et al., 2012; Alvadia et al., 2019), it was moderately selective for Na+ over Cl- (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations and shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Q559K mutant current showed minimal rundown in 1 mM Ca2+
source: In contrast, the mutant Q559K current recorded at +80 mV showed minimal rundown in 1 mM Ca2+, in spite of desensitization to Ca2+ activation (Figure 1B) (Alvadia et al., 2019; Ye et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1B,D.

claim: EC50 of Ca2+-activation for Q559K was shifted from 5.6 ± 0.3 µM to 52 ± 11 µM after 1-min-treatment of 1 mM Ca2+
source: Normalized to the respective maximal magnitudes of the currents before and after 1-min-treatment of 1 mM Ca2+, EC50 of Ca2+-activation was shifted from 5.6 ± 0.3 µM to 52 ± 11 µM (Figure 1C)
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The normalized fully activated current magnitude of Q559K was 0.89 ± 0.18
source: while the normalized fully activated current magnitude was 0.89 ± 0.18 (current in 1 mM Ca2+ normalized to that before 1 mM Ca2+), significantly different from 0.36 ± 0.13 for wild type (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Q559K in 1 mM Ca2+ has V1/2 of 18 ± 10 mV
source: but in 1 mM Ca2+ the left-shift overrode the effect of desensitization, with V1/2 being 18 ± 10 mV (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F,H).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F,H.

claim: The Erev of TMEM16F Q559K current activated by 1 mM Ca2+ was −14 ± 1 mV in 15 mM NaCl
source: Interestingly, the Erev of TMEM16F Q559K current activated by 1 mM Ca2+ exhibited a left-shift to −14 ± 1 mV in 15 mM NaCl, suggesting that it was more permeable to Cl- than to Na+ (Figure 1F,G)
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1F,G.

claim: The Erev of Q559K in 15 µM Ca2+ was 12 ± 2 mV
source: in contrast to 12 ± 2 mV as the Erev of it in 15 µM Ca2+ (recorded with the same protocol as for wild type above).
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The PNa+/PCl- of Q559K was 0.47 ± 0.03 in 1 mM Ca2+
source: Corrected for the liquid junction potential calculated with Clampex, these results indicated that the PNa+/PCl- was 0.47 ± 0.03 in 1 mM Ca2+, in contrast to 2.1 ± 0.4 as calculated from Erev in 15 µM Ca2+.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and calculated from reversal potential data.

claim: The PNa+/PCl- of Q559K was 2.1 ± 0.4 in 15 µM Ca2+
source: Corrected for the liquid junction potential calculated with Clampex, these results indicated that the PNa+/PCl- was 0.47 ± 0.03 in 1 mM Ca2+, in contrast to 2.1 ± 0.4 as calculated from Erev in 15 µM Ca2+.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and calculated from reversal potential data.

claim: Wild-type TMEM16F dynamically underwent the transition of an increased preference for Cl- permeation with the elevation of intracellular Ca2+ concentration
source: With this protocol, we found a left-shift of Erev accompanied with rapid current inactivation, until the current was too small to be distinguishable from endogenous current (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A,B,C). Thus, wild-type TMEM16F dynamically underwent the transition of an increased preference for Cl- permeation with the elevation of intracellular Ca2+ concentration.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: Q559W mutation prevents current rundown
source: It has been recently reported that mutation of Q559 to aromatic amino acids (such as Q559W) in TMEM16F also prevents current rundown (Nguyen et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citation to Nguyen et al., 2019.

claim: The Erev shift persisted in Q559W regardless of background subtraction
source: Although in each condition the Erev of Q559W was more positive than that of Q559K, the Erev shift persisted, regardless of background subtraction (with background currents recorded in Ca2+-free solutions with the same NaCl concentration) (Figure 1—figure supplement 4D,E,F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4D,E,F.

claim: TMEM16F is more permeable to I- than Cl-
source: Among anions, both wild-type TMEM16F and mutant channels are more permeable to I- than Cl- (Figure 1—figure supplement 5) (Nguyen et al., 2019)
evidence: This is stated in the results section with data in Figure 1—figure supplement 5 and citation.

claim: For each recording from either WT or Q559K, the current evoked by 6 µM Ca2+ reversed at a more positive voltage than that by 15 µM Ca2+
source: We found that for each recording from either WT or Q559K, the current evoked by 6 µM Ca2+ reversed at a more positive voltage than that by 15 µM Ca2+ (Figure 2A,B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2A,B,C.

claim: The EC50 of the double-mutant Q559K_E667Q was 0.88 ± 0.06 mM
source: The EC50 of the double-mutant, Q559K_E667Q, was 0.88 ± 0.06 mM, suggesting that the double mutant should not be in the fully open state in 1 mM Ca2+ (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2D,E.

claim: The current of Q559K_E667Q in 1 mM Ca2+ reversed at −6.9 ± 2.0 mV
source: Strikingly, the current in 1 mM Ca2+ reversed at −6.9 ± 2.0 mV, corresponding to a channel with higher permeability to Cl- than to Na+ (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2F.

claim: TMEM16F Q559K activation by 36 µM Ca2+ reached full or less-than-half open state, respectively, before or after desensitization
source: TMEM16F Q559K activation by 36 µM Ca2+ reached full or less-than-half open state, respectively, before or after desensitization (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1B,C.

claim: During the slow desensitization in 36 µM Ca2+, Erev remained unchanged despite the constant decrease of current magnitude and the increase of outward rectification
source: During the slow desensitization in 36 µM Ca2+, Erev (corrected with subtraction of background current recorded in 0 Ca2+ afterwards) remained unchanged despite the constant decrease of current magnitude and the increase of outward rectification.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3.

claim: The reversal potential of Q559K shifted only when Ca2+ concentration was changed, independently of current magnitude, open state, or rectification level
source: We therefore concluded that the reversal potential of Q559K shifted only when Ca2+ concentration was changed, independently of current magnitude, open state, or rectification level.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: PIP2 does not contribute to the shift of ion permeability ratio
source: Also, although it was not clear whether the permeation pathway could be partially composed of the headgroups of lipids being scrambled, we inferred that at least PIP2, which was slowly depleted during incubation in 36 µM Ca2+, did not contribute to the shift of ion permeability ratio.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and inferred from data in Figure 3.

claim: In TMEM16A, the glycine in TM6 (G640 or G644 depending on isoform) works as a hinge to allow the rearrangement of the helical segments during channel activation
source: In TMEM16A, the glycine in TM6 (G640 or G644 depending on isoform) works as a hinge to allow the rearrangement of the helical segments during channel activation to generate the ionic permeation pathway (Paulino et al., 2017a; Peters et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to structural studies.

claim: Alanine substitution of the glycine hinge in TMEM16A stabilizes TM6 at the open conformation and increases TMEM16A Ca2+ sensitivity
source: Alanine substitution of this glycine stabilizes TM6 at the open conformation and increases TMEM16A Ca2+ sensitivity (Paulino et al., 2017a; Peters et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to structural and functional studies.

claim: The glycine hinge in TMEM16A TM6 corresponds to G615 in TMEM16F
source: This glycine hinge in TMEM16A TM6 corresponds to G615 in TMEM16F according to sequence alignment (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: TM6 is bent at the glycine hinge (G615) in Ca2+-free but not Ca2+-bound TMEM16F
source: Cryo-EM studies reveal that TM6 is bent at this glycine hinge in Ca2+-free but not Ca2+-bound TMEM16F (Feng et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citation to Feng et al., 2019.

claim: G615A increases Ca2+ sensitivity of TMEM16F
source: Previous studies have shown that its alanine substitution (G615A) increases Ca2+ sensitivity (Alvadia et al., 2019; Han et al., 2019)
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to Alvadia et al., 2019 and Han et al., 2019.

claim: G615A left-shifted the voltage dependence of channels recorded in 15 μM Ca2+
source: and we confirmed that G615A left-shifted the voltage dependence of channels recorded in 15 μM Ca2+ (Figure 4A,D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4A,D.

claim: Mutation of G614A did not have similar or further effects as G615A
source: In contrast, mutation of the adjacent glycine, G614A, did not have similar or further effects (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E,F,G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E,F,G.

claim: TMEM16F I612A caused shifts in Ca2+- and voltage-gating by an extent comparable with those of G615A
source: TMEM16F I612A, mutation of the isoleucine in TM6 upper segment, caused shifts in Ca2+- and voltage-gating by an extent comparable with those of G615A (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D,G) (Han et al., 2019)
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D,G.

claim: Alanine substitution of N620 did not facilitate Ca2+ or voltage gating
source: alanine substitution of the asparagine '5-amino-acid-away' in TMEM16F TM6, N620, did not facilitate Ca2+ (Han et al., 2019) or voltage gating (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: The steady-state voltage dependence of TMEM16F G615A channel in 15 μM Ca2+ was comparable to that of Q559K in 1 mM Ca2+
source: Notably, the steady-state voltage dependence of TMEM16F G615A channel in 15 μM Ca2+ was comparable to that of Q559K in 1 mM Ca2+ (Figure 4A,D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4A,D.

claim: Q559K_G615A in 1 mM Ca2+ showed further left-shift of G-V relationship
source: We then generated the double-mutant Q559K_G615A, which in 1 mM Ca2+ showed further left-shift of G-V relationship (Figure 4B,C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4B,C,D.

claim: The change of the permeability ratio PNa+/PCl- with rising Ca2+ in Q559K_G615A was similar to that of Q559K (and wild-type) TMEM16F
source: The change of the permeability ratio PNa+/PCl- with rising Ca2+ in this double mutant was similar to that of Q559K (and wild-type) TMEM16F (Figure 4E,F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4E,F.

claim: TMEM16F channel in 15 μM Ca2+ was modestly more permeable to Na+, but it became more permeable to Cl- in 1 mM Ca2+ regardless of TM6 stabilization
source: This double mutant revealed that in the presence of Q559K mutation, TMEM16F channel in 15 μM Ca2+ was modestly more permeable to Na+, but it became more permeable to Cl- in 1 mM Ca2+ regardless of TM6 stabilization.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4E,F.

claim: TMEM16F ion selectivity more likely depends on intracellular Ca2+ concentration directly rather than its open state(s)
source: Taken together, these results suggest that TMEM16F ion selectivity more likely depends on intracellular Ca2+ concentration directly rather than its open state(s)
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by the collective data from mutants.

claim: Both Zn2+- and Gd3+-activations of TMEM16F were coupled with rapid inactivation even at low concentrations
source: Both Zn2+- and Gd3+-activations of TMEM16F were coupled with rapid inactivation even at low concentrations (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,D)
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,D.

claim: The exposure to divalent-free solution (with EGTA) for ~30 s to 1 min following channel inactivation by Zn2+ allowed the current to fully recover in magnitude
source: The exposure to divalent-free solution (with EGTA) for ~30 s to 1 min following channel inactivation by Zn2+ allowed the current to fully recover in magnitude (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C)
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: The rapid current rundown by Zn2+ was not attributed to desensitization triggered by PIP2 degradation
source: suggesting that the rapid current rundown was not attributed to desensitization triggered by PIP2 degradation, although it is unclear whether Zn2+ can shield the negative charges in PIP2 headgroups to elicit a reversible rundown.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and inferred from the reversibility data.

claim: Wild-type TMEM16F channels activated by 10 μM Zn2+ were more permeable to Na+ than to Cl-
source: We found that the wild-type TMEM16F channels activated by 10 μM Zn2+ were more permeable to Na+ than to Cl-, as evident from the right-shift in Erev as intracellular NaCl dropped to 15 mM (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: TMEM16F Q559K channels exhibited an increased relative permeability to Cl- (versus to Na+) with elevation of Zn2+ concentration from 10 μM to 1 mM
source: Notably, TMEM16F Q559K channels exhibited an increased relative permeability to Cl- (versus to Na+) with elevation of Zn2+ concentration from 10 μM to 1 mM (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5B,C.

claim: Wild-type TMEM16F current activated by Gd3+ underwent the Erev shift when Gd3+ concentration was switched from 10 µM to 1 mM
source: The remaining current underwent the Erev shift when Gd3+ concentration was switched from 10 µM to 1 mM (Figure 5D,E,F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5D,E,F.

claim: Wild-type TMEM16F current activated by Gd3+ showed weaker outward rectification compared with Ca2+-activated current
source: Note that wild-type TMEM16F current activated by Gd3+ showed weaker outward rectification (Figure 5E, compared with Figure 1—figure supplement 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The elevation of intracellular cation level underlies the increased permeability to Cl-, with divalent cations (Ca2+ and Zn2+) and trivalent cations (Gd3+) having stronger effects than monovalent ions (Na+ and NMDG)
source: Taken together, the elevation of intracellular cation level underlies the increased permeability to Cl-, with divalent cations (Ca2+ and Zn2+) and trivalent cations (Gd3+) having stronger effects than monovalent ions (Na+ and NMDG).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by the collective data from experiments with different cations.

claim: TMEM16F employs a charge-screening mechanism to dynamically alter the preference for permeating ion species
source: This suggests that TMEM16F employs a charge-screening mechanism to dynamically alter the preference for permeating ion species: Increase of positive charges, by introduction of basic amino acids or by entry of cations, enhances the channel preference for anions.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and inferred from the collective experimental evidence.

claim: The PNa+/PCl- values measured in 15 µM Ca2+ were 4.8 ± 0.6 and 2.3 ± 0.2 for wild-type TMEM16F in 15 mM and 45 mM NaCl, respectively
source: Indeed, the calculated PNa+/PCl- values measured in 15 µM Ca2+ were 4.8 ± 0.6 and 2.3 ± 0.2 for wild-type TMEM16F in 15 mM and 45 mM NaCl, respectively
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6.

claim: The PNa+/PCl- values measured in 15 µM Ca2+ were 2.1 ± 0.4 and 1.4 ± 0.1 for Q559K in 15 mM and 45 mM NaCl, respectively
source: and the calculated PNa+/PCl- values measured in 15 µM Ca2+ were 2.1 ± 0.4 and 1.4 ± 0.1 for Q559K in 15 mM and 45 mM NaCl, respectively (Figure 6)
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6.

claim: Q559K reduces PNa+/PCl-

claim: Controlling the selectivity between cations and anions by altering the pore potential is documented in other ion channels, such as ligand-gated channels and bacterial porins

evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to studies on other channels.
